chapter_title: Concerning the Summons, in which Limb of the Soul

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
The primal good poured itself outward and became scattered, and with it the living consciousness that should have remained unified broke into separated powers, so that it no longer recognized its own state. Yet the blessed Divine-Human approached in an unperceived way, entering that disorder by the likeness of His own order, by the form of His own life, by the warmth of His love, and by pure wisdom itself, the illumination of truth from the Divine.

As in a person the ruling principle holds every subordinate function in connection, so in the inner life every operative power depends on the supreme of order. If some lower function is injured or removed while the ruling principle remains, restoration is still possible; but if the ruling principle itself is rejected and severed, the whole organized life perishes and the state is lost.

So it was in that first spiritual state: the governing good was the ruling principle, and the derivative powers were the subordinate functions of its life meant to remain conjoined to it. And conversely, it was also like the general influx that gives vitality to everything in the outermost degree, by which all things there receive activity and continuance. This ruling principle was held in the highest degree of spiritual order, supported in its connection with the ultimate foundation of heaven by the sustaining Divine presence.

So too with the Father as the blessed Divine-Human: He is the supreme from which all organization proceeds, and He is the general influx that keeps all things in being; and He is set in the highest degree upon heaven’s ultimate foundation, made steadfast by pure wisdom that is from Him and is His living consciousness, with which He invests Himself for operation.

From Himself He brought forth and sent out sufficient operative powers by which His purpose could be accomplished below: the faculty that receives and arranges, the faculty that thinks and forms, the faculty that sees inwardly, the faculty that provides order for action, and the faculty that weighs and judges. He maintained pursuit of them by continual influx, for the things belonging to His living consciousness were entangled among those who resist order, and those entangled powers were like subordinate functions of that life bound within the ultimate domain.

When these powers had gone forth, He remained conjoined with pure wisdom, and from that union He rose into active intercession, asking that the needed strength be granted. Then the Divine granted tranquility and conjunction, and gave the certainty of restoration of the Divine-Human in that scattered condition. And the Divine-Human received power for the work: He restored the separated powers, gathered the dispersed consciousness back into order, and established it in its proper degree as a fixed structure of conjunction.

He then brought that restored consciousness into determinate form and perfected it with skill, arranging it according to the ordered expressions of truth He sent out, so that they might descend into what was opposed to good, extinguish the inflamed hostility, and raise up the consciousness that had been crushed by evil. The scattered powers were gathered back within; they returned and were made steadfast again, reformed into the likeness of their Divine source.

paragraph_translations.translation: The primal good poured itself outward and became scattered, and the living consciousness that depended on its unity was torn into separated powers, so that it no longer recognized what it had become. Yet the blessed Divine-Human approached in an unperceived way, entering that state by the likeness of His own order, by the form of His own life, by the warmth of His love, and by pure wisdom itself, the illumination of truth from the Divine.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES the chapter by stating the initial scattering and the secret advent of restoring Divinity.
paragraph_translations.notes: The clause about not knowing what he had become is syntactically broken in the source; translation follows the apparent sense.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: The chapter reads as one coherent movement: dispersal of unified life, the hidden approach of the restoring Divine-Human, a governing-principle analogy establishing the possibility of restoration, the sending out of operative faculties, intercession and granting of conjunction, and the re-formation and fixing of the scattered powers into ordered unity. Coherence is strongest in paragraphs 3–8; paragraph 2 has some textual fragmentation in the source but still yields a consistent spiritual narrative.

findings.diagnosis: Text is partially damaged/fragmentary, but the teaching voice and narrative function are coherent: it introduces dispersal/scattering and the hidden advent of the restoring figure. The reader’s only stumble is syntactic breakage, not a voice-intrusion or seam-expansion.
findings.evidence: Chapter text shows bracketed lacunae and broken syntax: “he [poured himself out and scattered] limb of the living soul… he has [the members] he did not know [what he had become]”. The spiritual reading explicitly flags this as the issue: “syntactically broken in the source; translation follows the apparent sense.” Despite damage, the content teaches by function (dispersal → loss of self-recognition; ‘came in secret’ → hidden restorative approach) rather than by jurisdiction, lists, or ranks. No administrative markers (no stations, authorities, territorial control, inventories). Removing any piece would not improve flow; the paragraph is the needed incipit to ¶3’s body-analogy.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: the head/limb analogy teaches restoration/loss by organic function, and it is the chapter’s governing explanatory hinge. No narrative break.
findings.evidence: “as the root of all the limbs hang upon the head… if his head should be cut off, the entire body will die” is classic functional correspondence: head functions as unifying principle; limbs as dependent operations; healing depends on head remaining. The spiritual reading reports no stumble and treats it as the law that makes the rest intelligible (“governing-principle law of restoration or loss”). Nothing here resembles Mani’s administrative layer (no named governors; no jurisdiction language).

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential teaching with a double analogy (head/limbs; air/breath). The “Pillar of Glory” placement remains functional (support/height/axis) rather than administrative. No insertion signal.
findings.evidence: “He is the head… his sons attach to it the limbs of his soul. Or, conversely, like the living air, on which all flesh entirely lives as it breathes…” This continues teaching by what things do: head unifies; air vivifies/sustains. The spiritual reading notes the double comparison and keeps it as complementary (“double comparison… retained”). “His head is placed on the body of the Pillar of Glory” reads as cosmological anatomy (support/axis) continuous with the body analogy, not as a territorial assignment or chain-of-command.

findings.diagnosis: Slight person/term pressure (“father, the blessed Man”) but still within the same correspondential framework: head/air strengthened by the Virgin of Light as ‘soul’ that he ‘clothes’. The reader’s difficulty is again fragmentation, not a voice change.
findings.evidence: Text: “the father, the blessed Man; as he is like the head… and the air… being made strong by his light virgin… who is his soul that he clothes [with her]”. This keeps the functional mapping (head/air; strengthening; clothing/investing) but the titulature (“father, the blessed Man”) compresses identities, which the reading notes: “source grammar is fragmentary.” Still, no administrative diagnostics appear (no ranks/jurisdictions). The narrative from ¶3–¶6 flows directly: governing principle → cosmic placement → same structure in the Father/Man pair.

findings.diagnosis: Correspondential list of inner powers/faculties; this is not an administrative inventory because the items are functional capacities, not named officials with jurisdictions. The list fits the narrative logic (sending operative powers to recover entangled soul).
findings.evidence: “those powers: the mind, thought, insight, counsel and consideration… produced and sent forth… to do his will” are capacities defined by function (thinking, seeing, judging), not governance. The paragraph immediately supplies functional purpose: “for the sake of his living soul, which is entwined among the rebels… like the limbs of its body.” The spiritual reading treats them exactly as operative faculties and reports no narrative stumble; it integrates them into the restorative process. This lacks Mani-layer markers like ‘authorities over’, ‘stations’, ‘watches’, named rulers, or territorial partitions.

findings.diagnosis: The only real stumble is agent alternation (Father/Man) creating momentary ambiguity, but it is narratively coherent as a restoration sequence (request → grant → gathering). This looks like source compression/damage rather than an insertion of a different voice.
findings.evidence: Text alternates: “he was found with the Virgin of Light… asking… [and the Father] gave him peace… tidings… The Man him[s]elf gave [power to gather] his limbs…” The spiritual reading flags this explicitly: “source alternates between speakers/agents (‘Father’ and ‘Man’).” However, the content remains functional: intercession, peace/kiss (conjunction), power to gather limbs/soul, building “like this tower.” There is no administrative jurisdictional content; the alternation is a coherence/identification issue, not a governance overlay. Excising any clause would not resolve the alternation without harming the narrative steps.

findings.diagnosis: Clean completion of the correspondential restoration: shaping/beautifying, ordering by ‘voices’, descending to quench ‘fire of wrath’, re-stabilizing gathered powers. No insertion signal.
findings.evidence: Text is process language: “shaped… beautified… form according to the voices… sink in and quench the fire of wrath… They were gathered in… set firm once more… in the image of their father.” The spiritual reading has no stumble and reads ‘voices’ as functional expressions of truth that effect descent and quenching. Nothing administrative appears (no ranks, enumerated jurisdictions, named officials). The narrative resolves smoothly from ¶6–¶8 (sent powers → empowered gathering → reformation).

textual_criticism.summary: No administrative overlay blocks and no clear seam-expansions are present. The chapter is overwhelmingly correspondential (¶3–¶4, ¶6, ¶8) with minor identity compression/agent alternation (¶5, ¶7) and clear textual damage in ¶2. The spiritual reading’s few stumbles arise from fragmentation and alternating agents, not from inserted administrative material. Recommendations: 0 excisions; 0 annotations; all paragraphs retained (¶2 diagnosed as damaged but coherent).

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Indeed, the First Man dispersed himself and he [poured himself out and scattered] limb of the living soul as I have written for you [each] of the living soul; he has [the members] he did not know [what he had become] but the blessed, glorious Man came [in] secret; in his image; in his shape; in his love; in his holy virgin, she who is the virgin of light, the soul of the father.

After the fashion of this fleshly body: as the root of all the limbs hang upon the head, so that should one of the person's limbs be cut off, while the head exists he has hope for [healing] but if his head should be cut off, the entire body will die and he is lost.

This is also the case for the Firs[t] Ma[n]. He is the head, while his sons attach to it the limbs [of] his soul. Or, conversely, like the living air, on which all flesh entirely lives as it breathes and [is sustained] therein. His head is placed on the body of the Pillar of Glory in the heights of the universe.

[This i]s also the case [for] the father, the blessed Man; as he is like the head that is upon the body and the air that upon the Pillar is set i[in the height] being made strong by his light virgin, [she] who is his soul that he clothes [with her]

[He brought forth] t[h]ose [powers]: the mind, thought, insight, counsel and c[on]sideration that he produced and sent forth from hi[m to] do his will. He sprang and travelled behind them. [for the sake] of his living soul, which is entwined among the rebels; as they are like the limbs of its body, and [bound in the body of the] universe.

And when they were sent, at [that ti]m[e] he was found with the Virgin of [Lig]ht and [he] stood up, asking and entreating for a p[o]wer. [and the Father] gave him peace and a ki[ss of peace] he [gave] him goo[d] tidings [concerning the restoration of the] Man. The Man him[s]elf gave [power to gather] his limbs and gathered his soul i[in its place] he built it in its place like this tower [of the heights]

[Then he] shaped it and beautified it skillfully [he] for[m according to] the voices that he sent [so that] he might sink in and quench [the fire of wrath] so[u]l that was crushed by the enemy. They were gathered in. They came, set firm once more, in the image of their father.
